Subject: SIG — encryption section: evidence request and clarifications

Hi Monica,

Thanks for agreeing to help with our SIG review. We are working through the encryption section and need some concrete evidence and clarifications to close this control area. High-level ask below — please attach any artifacts (PDFs, screenshots, rotation schedule) or point us to a secure link.

1) In-transit: brief statement of TLS versions supported, cipher suites disallowed, and whether mutual TLS is used for internal service-to-service traffic.
2) At-rest: which services use envelope encryption vs full-disk, and which KMS/CMK constructs are used.
3) Key custody: who has administrative access to customer master keys; confirm whether keys are in an HSM-backed KMS and whether you use cloud provider KMS or self-managed HSM.
4) Rotation: rotation frequency for master keys and data keys, automated vs manual processes, and the rotation proof artifacts (rotation schedule, rotation job logs).
5) Attestation: any HSM attestation or third-party reports demonstrating FIPS 140-2/3 compliance for your KMS/HSM environment.

Can you send the items as attachments or share a Drive folder by EOD Friday? If it helps, we can do a short technical call — Marcus from your team was super helpful on a past audit.

Appreciate it,
Jake

Subject: Re: SIG — encryption section: evidence request and clarifications

Jake — thanks for the clear list. Drafting answers below and attaching an evidence packet we maintain for SIG/SOC 2 reviews. See attachments: redwood_sig_encryption_evidence_v1.pdf (high-level statements + screenshots), kms_key_rotation_schedule.csv (rotation log summary), hsm-attestation-2026-06.pdf (vendor attestation).

Quick answers (summary):
- In transit: We terminate client TLS at our edge (TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported; we avoid legacy ciphers — see appendix A in the attached PDF). Service-to-service traffic within our VPC uses mTLS for consistency-controlled services; optional mTLS for partner connectors.
- At rest: Customer data is encrypted using an envelope encryption model. Application-level data keys are generated per-tenant, wrapped by a customer master key (CMK) stored in a KMS. For hosted customers we use the cloud provider KMS with HSM-backed keys (AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed CMKs). On private deployments we support customer-managed HSMs (bring-your-own HSM); the evidence PDF describes a couple of recent deployments.
- Key custody: CMKs are owned by Redwood, but access is limited via least-privilege IAM roles and split duties. No single operator has both KMS admin + signing privileges; access requires a documented approval workflow (see page 8 of PDF).
- Rotation: Master CMKs are on a 90-day rotation cadence by default for internal operational keys; data-encryption keys (DEKs) are rotated per usage pattern and rekeyed automatically on tenant-specific milestones. Rotation is automated for hosted customers; for private deployments rotation can be scheduled through the ops console and can be customer-triggered. Rotation schedule export attached.
- Attestation: The attached hsm-attestation-2026-06.pdf is our latest vendor attestation demonstrating HSM-backed key material and FIPS-related controls. We also retain audit logs for KMS operations and can provide filtered extracts under NDA if needed.

If you want deeper technical details (KMS key policy snippets, CloudHSM cluster topology, rotation job logs), I can pull those with Marcus — looping him in. Would you prefer a 30-minute call tomorrow or an artifact-only handoff?

Thanks,
Monica
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Jake, Monica — looping in the technical details requested. Short answers followed by pointers to artifacts in the Drive link Monica shared.

- BYOK support: Yes. Hosted customers can request a BYOK CMK. Onboarding is initiated via a security request form (link in Drive). The process: generate a key material envelope on the customer side, provide a public key blob to our onboarding service, we wrap the provided key material into the customer CMK and import it into a dedicated CloudHSM key slot when requested. Onboarding steps and role approvals are documented in the onboarding playbook (Drive).

- Rotation evidence: We export rotation events with job IDs and non-sensitive metadata. Example (redacted) rotation events for CMK-abc123: job-id rot-20260501-9f2a (completed), rot-20260531-4e1c (completed), rot-20260630-0b7d (completed). The kms_key_rotation_schedule.csv attached in Monica's message contains a similar export; full job logs can be provided under an executed DPA/NDA.

- HSM tenancy and logs: We operate a pooled HSM model for our hosted environment (CloudHSM clusters partitioned by tenant via logical separation). For private deployments we recommend single-tenant HSM appliances (customer-owned). We ingest HSM events into our immutable audit pipeline; logs include timestamp, operation, and operator service account id. Access to raw HSM logs is controlled and provided only under contractual agreements.

- Practical note on rotation frequency: operational CMKs rotate on a 90-day automated cadence. DEKs are rotated per-tenant on lifecycle events (rekey after export/import, or upon privilege change). All rotation jobs emit an audit record and push a rotation-complete marker to the audit stream.

I attached a sample key-policy snippet and a sanitized rotation-job export to the shared Drive folder. If you need a redacted log sample in-line, I can paste one here or schedule a short call.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
